domain: Facebook/Meta paid advertising — targeting the known West Side Bend homeowner CRM segment
summary: I re-verified every cited path from source. The prior audit was substantially accurate on reachability — no hallucinated file paths, and the two dead-code findings (getAdAudienceConversionReport, uploadOfflineConversion) are confirmed with zero callers. I confirmed live production state directly: META_AUDIENCE_PUSH_ENABLED="true" is genuinely set in Vercel production (verified by pulling the env, not by trusting a doc), so the daily "Ryan Realty CRM Leads" sync is really pushing — and it really does push the entire non-suppressed CRM book with no geography filter, while the West Side audience (id 120244510092910698) is refreshed only by a hand-typed CLI command. Two things the prior audit missed entirely: (1) a REAL, wired CRM-stage → Meta CAPI "Qualified" feedback loop exists at app/actions/crm.ts:1237 → lib/meta/qualifiedEvent.ts, which makes its "the closed loop has never fired" framing incomplete — though I confirmed META_CAPI_QUALIFIED_ENABLED is absent from production env, so it is hard dry-run and has in fact never sent a real event; (2) the campaign-level suppression/exclusion audience and the lookalike seed the playbook mandates have NO code at all anymore (the only builder, scripts/export-fub-custom-audience.mjs, was deleted), so every prospecting ad set is paying to reacquire people already in the CRM with nothing in-repo to prevent it. I downgraded the auditor's "have" on identity resolution to partial: the audience sync's own DAL read supports a tag filter that would produce the West Side audience correctly, and nobody uses it — the split the auditor called a wiring gap is one argument wide.

items.requirement: Sync the known West Side Bend homeowner CRM segment to a Meta Custom Audience for direct ad targeting
items.evidence: scripts/meta-refresh-westside-audience.mjs:44 hard-codes AUDIENCE_ID = '120244510092910698' ("RR Westside Bend Homeowners") and pushes at line 191 to graph.facebook.com/v21.0/<id>/users. grep for 'meta-refresh-westside-audience' across the whole repo returns ONLY the script's own header comments (lines 3, 33, 34) — zero callers, not in vercel.json, not in package.json scripts. The daily job is a different audience: app/api/cron/meta-audience-sync/route.ts (vercel.json:180-182, '0 9 * * *') calls syncCrmAudience() in lib/meta/audienceUpload.ts, whose CRM_AUDIENCE_NAME constant (line 51) is 'Ryan Realty CRM Leads'. Its read, lib/data/crm/getAudienceEligiblePeople.ts:153-158, selects from crm_people with ONLY .eq('deleted', false) — no city, no geo, no parcel join; the only filters applied are contactable-key, crm_suppressions, and a realtor-tag exclusion (lines 168-184). I confirmed the live flag by pulling production env directly: META_AUDIENCE_PUSH_ENABLED="true".
items.gap: [VERIFIED] Confirmed, and worse than described. getAudienceEligiblePeople.ts:126-129 already accepts an optional `tag` filter, and lines 189-193 apply it — and scripts/_westside-insert-netnew.mjs:52 and scripts/_westside-enrich-contacts.mjs:77 already stamp the tag 'farm:westside' onto exactly these people. The daily cron at app/api/cron/meta-audience-sync/route.ts:57 calls syncCrmAudience({ dryRun }) with no tag. The West Side segment is one argument away from being the automatically-refreshed audience and nobody passed it. Meanwhile the audience that IS live-refreshed daily is the entire CRM book.
items.why_it_matters: The one thing Matt asked for — target our known West Side homeowners — is the only audience in the system that nothing keeps fresh.

items.requirement: Confirm the homeowner Custom Audience is actually usable as an inclusion targeting option under Meta's mandatory Housing Special Ad Category
items.evidence: docs/plans/ADS_GO_LIVE.md launch step 2 reads verbatim: 'New campaign → Special Ad Category = Housing → open the audience selector → check whether "Ryan Realty CRM Leads" is selectable for inclusion. Lookalikes are NOT usable under Housing (confirmed)'. Step 3 hedges the same way: 'the Custom Audience if step 2 says it's allowed'. Code-side, lib/meta-marketing-api.mjs:191 and :236 hard-set special_ad_categories: ['HOUSING'] on both campaign and ad-set creation, so the constraint is enforced in code but the audience-compatibility question is never touched. Nothing later in the repo resolves it.
items.gap: [VERIFIED] Confirmed unresolved. Note this is the ONE item where a doc is legitimately the evidence, because the question is about Meta's platform behavior, not our code — it cannot be answered from source at all. It is a 2-minute check in Ads Manager that gates the value of every other item in this report.
items.why_it_matters: If inclusion targeting is blocked under Housing, the West Side audience is only usable for exclusion/retargeting and the entire strategy changes shape.

items.requirement: Campaign / ad set / ad structure managed per Facebook best practices (CBO, 3-campaign architecture, exclusions, creative rotation)
items.evidence: lib/meta-marketing-api.mjs implements createCampaign (line 180+), createAdSet (line ~236), lead form, creative, ad, and status flow with HOUSING enforced. grep -rl 'meta-marketing-api' across the repo returns exactly four files: scripts/create-fb-ad.mjs (the manual CLI), lib/lead-form-template.mjs, lib/meta-graph.ts, and the module itself. I opened the lib/meta-graph.ts hit — it is a COMMENT at line 1051 ('consistent with the existing lib/meta-marketing-api.mjs conventions'), not an import. There is no app/api/admin/meta-* route directory at all, and grep for any Graph write to /campaigns, /adsets, or /ads under app/ or lib/ returns nothing.
items.gap: [VERIFIED] Confirmed — the auditor's single non-import hit in lib/meta-graph.ts was a comment, and it did not claim otherwise. No code creates or reconciles live campaign structure. Consistent with the CLAUDE.md producer-freeze, so likely intentional, but it means the live account cannot be verified against the locked strategy from code.

items.requirement: Suppression/exclusion audience and lookalike seed pushed to Meta so prospecting ad sets stop paying to reacquire existing CRM contacts
items.evidence: docs/FB_SELLER_CAMPAIGN_PLAYBOOK.md:21 mandates 'upload the FUB suppression CSV (built via scripts/export-fub-custom-audience.mjs --mode suppression) as an Exclusion on every campaign', and :16 mandates a lookalike seeded via --mode lookalike-seed. `ls scripts/export-fub-custom-audience.mjs` → No such file. Nothing replaced it: grep for 'suppression' under lib/meta/ returns only comments in audienceUpload.ts:7,52 and audienceLedger.ts:17 describing suppression as an EXCLUSION FROM the inclusion audience — not as a separate exclusion audience pushed to Meta. lib/meta/audienceRemove.ts removes people from the CRM inclusion audience; it does not build an exclusion file.
items.gap: [CORRECTED: the auditor did not cover this requirement at all — it appears only as a passing mention inside its stale-docs item.] There is now ZERO code in the repo that produces a Meta exclusion audience or a lookalike seed. The playbook's own stated waste-prevention control ('paying for a lead you already have is pure waste') has no implementation. ADS_GO_LIVE.md separately notes lookalikes are unusable under Housing anyway, so only the exclusion half is recoverable — and it is gone.
items.why_it_matters: Every dollar of prospecting spend can currently be served to the 13k+ people already in the CRM, with nothing in-repo preventing it.

items.requirement: An accurate, current playbook for launching/verifying the seller campaign
items.evidence: Verified each stale reference by opening the docs: docs/FB_SELLER_CAMPAIGN_PLAYBOOK.md:16, :21, :195, :196 all instruct running scripts/export-fub-custom-audience.mjs, which does not exist on disk. :253-254 instruct `curl -u "$UNUSED_VENDOR_CRM_KEY:" https://retired.invalid/v1/people?source=Facebook` as the verification step. docs/FACEBOOK_SELLER_GROWTH_PIPELINE.md:167 still lists UNUSED_VENDOR_CRM_KEY and UNUSED_VENDOR_CRM_PIPELINE as required env vars, :394 awards +15 health points for 'FUB API key configured', :533 describes it as the live 'FUB People + Events + Notes + Tasks' surface, and :714 describes the deleted export script as shipping. Source contradicts all of it: app/api/meta/lead-webhook/route.ts:16-22 documents that FUB was decommissioned 2026-06-24 and that the FUB push paths were dead no-ops silently dropping every webhook lead until replaced by the native chain.

items.requirement: Closed-loop conversion signal: lead becomes qualified/client → reported back to Meta for optimization
items.evidence: TWO paths, both non-firing, only one of which the prior audit found. (a) Offline conversions: lib/meta-offline-conversions.ts:77 uploadOfflineConversion() is correctly implemented (SHA-256 hashing, fbc key, event_id idempotency, action_source 'system_generated' — all four asserted by the gate scripts/check-tracking-policy.mjs:145-153). Its only importer is app/api/admin/offline-conversion/route.ts:21,51; a repo-wide grep for 'offline-conversion' finds no fetch() caller, no UI button, and docs/plans/ADMIN_REBUILD/audit-reports/_summary.json:2053 lists the route as 'superseded'. (b) MISSED BY THE PRIOR AUDIT: a real CRM-stage→CAPI loop is wired. app/actions/crm.ts:26 imports isQualifyingStage/fireQualifiedLeadEvent and line 1237 fires it on a stage transition INTO a qualifying stage. lib/meta/qualifiedEvent.ts:51-105 hashes PII, applies LDU for suppressed subjects, and uses event_id `qualified:<personId>:<stage>`. But line 82 hard-gates on isMetaCapiQualifiedEnabled() (lib/meta-env.ts:76-77, requires META_CAPI_QUALIFIED_ENABLED === 'true') and returns 'flag-disabled' otherwise. I pulled production env directly: META_CAPI_QUALIFIED_ENABLED is NOT PRESENT. Every stage change logs '[qualified-capi] DRY RUN (flag off)' and makes no Meta call.
items.gap: [CORRECTED: the auditor missed the entire fireQualifiedLeadEvent path, so its 'nothing in the CRM stage-change path invokes any Meta feedback' claim is wrong — the hook exists and is genuinely wired at app/actions/crm.ts:1237.] The net verdict is unchanged though: neither path has ever sent a real event. Offline conversions have no caller at all; the qualified loop has a caller but is flag-disabled in production, exactly as ADS_GO_LIVE.md instructs ('leave OFF for now'). So the wiring work is much smaller than the auditor implied — flipping one env var turns on a real feedback signal today.
items.why_it_matters: Meta cannot optimize toward lead QUALITY on zero quality events; flipping one flag is a far cheaper fix than the auditor's 'build a trigger hook' framing.

items.requirement: Identity resolution: a Facebook ad click/lead-form fill by a known CRM contact is recognized as the same person, not a duplicate
items.evidence: The mechanism is real and I verified each leg. app/api/meta-capi/route.ts is fetched from exactly 9 lead-capture action files (grep count = 9): app/contact/actions.ts:186, app/home-valuation/actions.ts:334, app/lp/seller-home-value/actions.ts:685, app/lp/fsbo/actions.ts:388, app/lp/expired-listing/actions.ts, app/lp/buyer-listing-alerts/actions.ts, app/lp/tetherow/heath/actions.ts, app/actions/lead-capture.ts, app/actions/lead-landing.ts. app/api/meta/lead-webhook/route.ts:1-9 imports sendEvent + ensureNativeLead/enrichNativeLead/createNativeTask and HMAC-verifies X-Hub-Signature-256 against META_APP_SECRET. lib/data/crm/ensureNativeLead.ts:72-97 implements the documented precedence: email match wins → reuse, never create; else phone match → reuse; matched against crm_contact_points.
items.gap: [CORRECTED: downgraded from 'have' to 'partial'.] The dedup logic is sound, but two reachability caveats the auditor did not flag. First, the webhook only receives anything if the Meta App Dashboard has the 'leadgen' Page field subscribed — that is external config the repo cannot assert, and app/api/meta/lead-webhook/route.ts:40-46 documents it as a one-time manual setup step with a callback URL still pointing at ryanrealty.vercel.app rather than the production domain ryan-realty.com (memory project_domain: the vercel.app host redirects). Second, route.ts:64-71 prefers META_USER_ACCESS_TOKEN and warns in its own comment that falling back to the Page token means inbound leads arrive with NO email/phone — which would defeat email-first dedup entirely. META_USER_ACCESS_TOKEN is present in production env (verified), so the fallback is not currently active, but the webhook callback URL discrepancy is unresolved.
items.why_it_matters: A webhook callback URL on the redirecting vercel.app host is exactly the class of misconfiguration that silently drops every FB lead-form submission.
